\end{aligned}

Hence, electron jumps from $\mathrm{n}_{2}=3$ to $\mathrm{n}_{1}=1$

questions.q: Two identical conducting balls $A$ and $B$ have positive charges $\mathrm{q}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{q}_{2}$ respectively but $\mathrm{q}_{1} \neq \mathrm{q}_{2}$. The balls are brought together so that they touch each other and then kept in their original positions. The force between them is
options: less than that before the balls touched
greater than that before the balls touched
same as that before the balls touched
questions.solution:
Original charges on spheres $A$ and $B$ be $\mathrm{q}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{q}_{2}$ respectively.
Distance between the two spheres $=\mathrm{r}$
Since, both the spheres are of same size, they will possess equal charges on being brought in contact.
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{q}_{1}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{1}+\mathrm{q}_{2}}{2}$
Similarly, $\quad \mathrm{q}_{2}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{1}+\mathrm{q}_{2}}{2}$
Therefore, new force of repulsion between spheres A and B is

\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{F}^{\prime} &=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0}} \frac{\left[\frac{\mathrm{q}_{1}+\mathrm{q}_{2}}{2}\right]\left[\frac{\mathrm{q}_{1}+\mathrm{q}_{2}}{2}\right]}{\mathrm{r}^{2}} \\
&=\frac{\left[\frac{\mathrm{q}_{1}+\mathrm{q}_{2}}{2}\right]^{2}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{r}^{2}} \\
\therefore & \text { As } \quad\left[\frac{\mathrm{q}_{1}+\mathrm{q}_{2}}{2}\right]^{2}>\mathrm{q}_{1} \mathrm{q}_{2} \\
\therefore & \mathrm{F}^{\prime}>\mathrm{F}
\end{aligned}

questions.q: A closed organ pipe and an open organ pipe of same length produce 2 beats/second while vibrating in their fundamental modes. The length of the open organ pipe is halved and that of closed pipe is doubled. Then the number of beats produced per second while vibrating in the fundamental mode is
questions.solution:
Given, $\quad \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}-\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}=2 \quad \text{...(i)}$ 
Frequency of fundamental mode for a closed Frequency of fundar organ pipe, $f_{c}=\frac{v}{4 L_{c}}$
Similarly frequency of fundamental mode for an open organ pipe, $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{2 \mathrm{~L}_{\mathrm{o}}}$
Given $\quad \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{c}}=\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{o}}\Rightarrowf_{0}=2 f_{c} \quad \text{...(ii)}$
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get 
$\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}=2 \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}=4 \mathrm{~Hz}$ and $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}=2 \mathrm{~Hz}$ 
When the length of the open pipe is halved, frequency of fundamental mode is  \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{2\left[\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{o}}}{2}\right]}=2 \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}=2 \times 4 \mathrm{~Hz}=8 \mathrm{~Hz} 
When the length of the closed pipe is doubled, its frequency of fundamental mode is

\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4\left(2 \mathrm{~L}_{\mathrm{c}}\right)}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{1}{2} \times 2=1 \mathrm{~Hz}

Hence, number of beats produced per second is

\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}^{\prime}-\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}^{\prime}=8-1=7
